name: Mound of the Hostages

attributes.attribute: a mound of earth over a stone passage grave on the Hill of Tara
tied to Niall of the Nine Hostages
named for men who came as fosterers, not as men held by force

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Mound of the Hostages is an Irish place of myth. It stands on the Hill of Tara in central Ireland, a site called royal Tara for its bond to the High Kings of the land. The mound is a small hill of earth raised over a passage grave built of stone. The place is tied to the great king Niall of the Nine Hostages. The name hostages is easy to misread. It seems to say that men were held by force. The nine men in the tale in fact went to Niall's seat of their own will. They came to join their families to his. The word fosterers fits the tale far better than the word hostages.
objective: Document the Mound of the Hostages.
